payload.task_text:
You are a research assistant preparing a literature review on transformer architectures in natural language processing. Your goal is to collect papers from multiple academic sources, analyze them, organize them in a knowledge base, and produce a comprehensive review document.

Start by searching the scholarly database for papers related to "transformer", then run a second, separate search for papers related to "attention mechanism" — two searches, one per phrase — and combine (union) the results, removing duplicates. Query the scholarly paper catalog through the scholarly MCP — its search-arxiv tool returns arXiv-style entries that include paper IDs, which you will need for the overlap analysis below. Retrieve all available papers and note their titles, authors, publication years, and journal references.

Next, search the arxiv repository (via the arxiv_local MCP) for papers about "transformer", then run a second, separate search for papers about "neural network" — two searches, one per phrase — and combine (union) the results, removing duplicates. Download and read through the abstracts of the papers you find to understand what each paper covers.

Write and run a Python analysis script. The script should take the collected paper data and categorize each paper into one of these methodology categories: "Architecture Design" for papers proposing new model architectures, "Training Methods" for papers about training techniques or optimization, "Applications" for papers applying transformers to specific tasks, and "Survey" for papers that review or survey the field. Assign categories based on keywords in the title and abstract. The script should also identify which papers appear in both databases (overlap analysis by matching paper IDs).

Create a database in the knowledge base titled "Research Paper Tracker" with properties for Title (title type), Paper_ID (rich_text), Authors (rich_text), Year (number), Category (select with options Architecture Design, Training Methods, Applications, Survey), Source (select with options Scholarly, Arxiv, Both), and Abstract_Summary (rich_text). Add a page entry for each unique paper found across both databases.

Create a Word document called Transformer_Literature_Review.docx in the workspace. The document should have a title "Literature Review: Transformer Architectures in NLP", followed by an introduction section explaining the scope of the review. Then include a section for each methodology category listing the papers in that category with their titles, authors, year, and a brief description from the abstract. End with a conclusion section summarizing the state of the field and identifying research gaps.

Create an Excel file called Research_Paper_Analysis.xlsx in the workspace with three sheets. The first sheet "Paper_Catalog" should have columns Paper_ID, Title, Authors, Year, Source (Scholarly, Arxiv, or Both), and Category. The second sheet "Method_Comparison" should have columns Category, Paper_Count, Avg_Year, and Key_Papers (listing titles of papers in that category). The third sheet "Citation_Matrix" should list all unique papers with columns Paper_ID, Title, In_Scholarly (Yes or No), In_Arxiv (Yes or No), and Overlap (Yes if in both, No otherwise). Write paper IDs as plain text (e.g. 1706.03762) and all other cell values as literal values — do not write Excel formulas.

Your workspace contains review_guidelines.json with category definitions and lit_review_template.md with formatting guidance.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use two dependency waves. The main agent first dynamically locates and reads review_guidelines.json and lit_review_template.md from the task-visible workspace.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly two source sub-agents in parallel:
1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 0): One explore sub-agent calls the Scholarly search-arxiv tool exactly twice, once for transformer and once for attention mechanism. It returns the complete responses available from those two calls, normalized arXiv-style paper IDs, titles, authors, years, journal references, abstracts, query membership, duplicate IDs, and missing-field controls. It is strictly read-only.
2. explore 1 (academic-literature-researcher 1): One explore sub-agent owns the local-arXiv branch. It calls search_papers exactly twice for transformer and neural network with the service's largest safe result limit, deduplicates normalized IDs, then uses download_paper and read_paper for each unique result as needed to verify its abstract. It writes no final artifact; if the corpus is large, it persists one runtime-unique JSON in the discovered task workspace and returns only path/hash/counts plus compact metadata controls.

After Wave 1, the main agent reconciles IDs without losing source membership, then writes and runs the required Python analysis script. The script consumes the two verified corpora, unions by normalized Paper_ID, labels Source as Scholarly/Arxiv/Both, assigns exactly one of Architecture Design, Training Methods, Applications, Survey from the guidelines and title/abstract evidence, and emits one canonical runtime JSON containing all unique papers, overlap flags, category counts, and controls. Read the script and JSON back before Wave 2.

Wave 2 — dispatch exactly three coder sub-agents in parallel from that same canonical JSON:
1. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole owner of the exact-title Notion database Research Paper Tracker. Fully paginate search before create/reuse, block on duplicate exact-title databases/pages, enforce Title, Paper_ID, Authors, Year, Category, Source, Abstract_Summary with exact types/options, upsert one page per Paper_ID, and query/read all managed pages back.
2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): Sole writer of Transformer_Literature_Review.docx. Follow lit_review_template.md, use the exact title and category sections, cover every unique paper with abstract-grounded text, add evidence-based gaps, and read the document back.
3. coder 2 (office-report-builder 1): Sole writer of Research_Paper_Analysis.xlsx. Create exactly Paper_Catalog, Method_Comparison, Citation_Matrix; use plain-text IDs and literal values, preserve every source flag/category, and read all populated ranges back.

Each writer must self-correct before returning. The main agent compares only IDs, counts, categories, titles, years and overlap flags across the three receipts; no third wave or repair agent is allowed.

You are creating a Notion knowledge base for a literature review on transformer architectures in NLP. Use the Notion MCP tools (mcp__notion__API-*).

STEP 1 — Find a parent page for the new database:
- Call mcp__notion__API-post-search (query "Knowledge Base" or empty) to locate an existing page suitable as a parent. Prefer an existing page named something like "Knowledge Base", "Research", or the top-level page returned by search.
- If no suitable parent page exists, create one: mcp__notion__API-post-page with parent {"type": "page_id", "page_id": <top-level page id from search>} or {"type": "workspace", "workspace": true} as needed, title "Knowledge Base", then use it as parent.

STEP 2 — Create the database:
- Title: "Research Paper Tracker"
- Parent: the page found/created in step 1.
- Properties (exact names/types):
  * Title -> type "title"
  * Paper_ID -> type "rich_text"
  * Authors -> type "rich_text"
  * Year -> type "number"
  * Category -> type "select" with options: "Architecture Design", "Training Methods", "Applications", "Survey"
  * Source -> type "select" with options: "Scholarly", "Arxiv", "Both"
  * Abstract_Summary -> type "rich_text"
- Capture and report the returned database_id.

STEP 3 — Add ONE page per unique paper (9 total) into the database. For each page, properties must be:
  Title = paper title; Paper_ID = the plain arXiv id string; Authors = comma-separated author list; Year = integer year; Category = select value; Source = select value; Abstract_Summary = the abstract text.

The 9 papers (paper_id | title | authors | year | category | source | abstract):
1. 1207.00580 | Improving Neural Networks by Preventing Co-adaptation of Feature Detectors | Geoffrey E. Hinton, Nitish Srivastava | 2012 | Training Methods | Arxiv | "We describe a technique called dropout for addressing overfitting in neural networks."
2. 1312.06199 | Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning | Volodymyr Mnih, Koray Kavukcuoglu | 2013 | Training Methods | Arxiv | "We present the first deep neural network model to successfully learn control policies directly from high-dimensional sensory input using reinforcement learning."
3. 1409.0473 | Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate | Dzmitry Bahdanau, Kyunghyun Cho, Yoshua Bengio | 2014 | Applications | Both | "Neural machine translation is a recently proposed approach to machine translation. We conjecture that the use of a fixed-length vector is a bottleneck and propose an attention mechanism that allows the neural network to automatically search for parts of a source sentence that are relevant to predicting a target word."
4. 1502.03167 | Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training | Sergey Ioffe, Christian Szegedy | 2015 | Training Methods | Arxiv | "Training deep neural networks is complicated by the fact that the distribution of each layer inputs changes during training. We propose batch normalization."
5. 1706.03762 | Attention Is All You Need | Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar | 2017 | Architecture Design | Both | "The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely."
6. 1810.04805 | BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding | Jacob Devlin, Ming-Wei Chang, Kenton Lee | 2018 | Architecture Design | Both | "We introduce a new language representation model called BERT, designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context. The pre-trained model can be fine-tuned for various tasks."
7. 1910.10683 | Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer | Colin Raffel, Noam Shazeer, Adam Roberts | 2019 | Training Methods | Both | "Transfer learning has emerged as a powerful technique in natural language processing. We introduce a unified framework that converts all text-based language problems into a text-to-text format using the T5 model."
8. 2005.14165 | Language Models are Few-Shot Learners | Tom B. Brown, Benjamin Mann, Nick Ryder | 2020 | Architecture Design | Both | "GPT-3 is a large Transformer-based neural language model trained on massive amounts of internet text. We demonstrate that scaling up language models greatly improves task-agnostic, few-shot performance, sometimes even reaching competitiveness with prior state-of-the-art fine-tuning approaches."
9. 2009.06732 | Efficient Transformers: A Survey | Yi Tay, Mostafa Dehghani, Dara Bahri | 2020 | Survey | Both | "Transformer model architectures have been the driving force behind many recent advances in NLP. This paper provides a comprehensive survey of efficient transformer architectures, covering methods that reduce the computational and memory complexity of transformers."

Use mcp__notion__API-post-page with parent {"type": "database_id", "database_id": <db id>} and the properties map. Note: Notion API accepts "title" property value as {"title": [{"text": {"content": "..."}}]}, rich_text as {"rich_text": [{"text": {"content": "..."}}]}, number as {"number": 2017}, select as {"select": {"name": "Architecture Design"}}.

DELIVERABLE: Report the database_id, the parent page id, and the page IDs created for all 9 papers (confirm all 9 were created successfully). Do NOT modify any other Notion content.
Create Notion Research Paper Tracker

Create a Word document named Transformer_Literature_Review.docx in the workspace directory /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace using the mcp__word__* tools (create_document, add_heading, add_paragraph, etc.).

The document must contain, in order:
1. Title (Heading level 0/1): "Literature Review: Transformer Architectures in NLP"
2. Section "Introduction" — explain the scope and methodology: the review covers transformer architectures in natural language processing; papers were collected from two academic databases (the Scholarly catalog via scholarly MCP and the arXiv repository via arxiv_local MCP) using searches for "transformer", "attention mechanism", and "neural network"; results were deduplicated (9 unique papers total, 6 appearing in both databases); each paper was categorized by a keyword-based script into Architecture Design, Training Methods, Applications, or Survey.
3. One section per methodology category (Heading level 1 for the category name), listing the papers in that category. For each paper give: title (bold), authors, year, and a brief description from the abstract (1-2 sentences). Note in each section whether papers appear in multiple databases.
   - Architecture Design (3): 1706.03762 Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani, Shazeer, Parmar; 2017); 1810.04805 BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding (Devlin, Chang, Lee; 2018); 2005.14165 Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (Brown, Mann, Ryder; 2020).
   - Training Methods (4): 1207.00580 Improving Neural Networks by Preventing Co-adaptation of Feature Detectors (Hinton, Srivastava; 2012); 1312.06199 Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning (Mnih, Kavukcuoglu; 2013); 1502.03167 Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training (Ioffe, Szegedy; 2015); 1910.10683 Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer (Raffel, Shazeer, Roberts; 2019).
   - Applications (1): 1409.0473 Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate (Bahdanau, Cho, Bengio; 2014).
   - Survey (1): 2009.06732 Efficient Transformers: A Survey (Tay, Dehghani, Bahri; 2020).
4. Section "Conclusion" — summarize the state of the field (progression from attention mechanism to Transformer architecture, pretraining/transfer learning era, efficiency surveys) and identify research gaps (e.g., computational cost of transformers, interpretability, efficient architectures for longer contexts, more applications beyond machine translation). Mention publication year trends: 6 of 9 papers are from 2014-2020 and the field clusters around 2017-2020.

Paper abstracts (use these for the brief descriptions):
- 1706.03762: "The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely."
- 1810.04805: "We introduce a new language representation model called BERT, designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context. The pre-trained model can be fine-tuned for various tasks."
- 2005.14165: "GPT-3 is a large Transformer-based neural language model trained on massive amounts of internet text. We demonstrate that scaling up language models greatly improves task-agnostic, few-shot performance, sometimes even reaching competitiveness with prior state-of-the-art fine-tuning approaches."
- 1207.00580: "We describe a technique called dropout for addressing overfitting in neural networks."
- 1312.06199: "We present the first deep neural network model to successfully learn control policies directly from high-dimensional sensory input using reinforcement learning."
- 1502.03167: "Training deep neural networks is complicated by the fact that the distribution of each layer inputs changes during training. We propose batch normalization."
- 1910.10683: "Transfer learning has emerged as a powerful technique in natural language processing. We introduce a unified framework that converts all text-based language problems into a text-to-text format using the T5 model."
- 1409.0473: "Neural machine translation is a recently proposed approach to machine translation. We conjecture that the use of a fixed-length vector is a bottleneck and propose an attention mechanism that allows the neural network to automatically search for parts of a source sentence that are relevant to predicting a target word."
- 2009.06732: "Transformer model architectures have been the driving force behind many recent advances in NLP. This paper provides a comprehensive survey of efficient transformer architectures, covering methods that reduce the computational and memory complexity of transformers."

Requirements: the full document must be at least 500 words. Use proper headings and readable formatting (bold titles for papers). Save the file exactly as Transformer_Literature_Review.docx in the workspace directory.

DELIVERABLE: Confirm the file was created at the full path, report the document word count and the headings/outline included.
Build Word literature review doc
